native_mechanisms: A single rolling sphere is the sole carried memory across the whole ordered pile of marks (one streaming accumulator, marks taken strictly in order, old face discarded).

Each mark is pressed into the sphere and then mixed by a fixed count of tumbles down the mason trail — the crack angle read at the stalk is the weight carried forward (fixed rotation-style mixing per byte, no multiplication).

Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is kept as the token; the sphere, intermediate cracks and dust are swept away (a terminal finalisation step on the accumulator, intermediate state discarded).
core_technique: Multiply-free rotating hash: per byte, add into a single 64-bit accumulator then rotate left by a fixed odd constant (11), 8x-unrolled, followed by Thomas Wang's shift/add/xor 64-bit finalizer on the final state.
